symbols.name: \(n\)
symbols.def: Common sample size in each randomized treatment arm.

symbols.name: \(m\)
symbols.def: Fold size \(m=n/2\).

symbols.name: \(i\)
symbols.def: Unit index within an arm.

symbols.name: \(d\)
symbols.def: Dimension of the conditioning covariate; \(d=0\) denotes the no-covariate branch.

symbols.name: \(s_y\)
symbols.def: H\"older smoothness in the outcome coordinate.

symbols.name: \(s_z\)
symbols.def: H\"older smoothness in the covariate coordinates when \(d\ge1\).

symbols.name: \(\alpha\)
symbols.def: Nominal noncoverage probability.

symbols.name: \(c\)
symbols.def: Uniform density lower bound.

symbols.name: \(C\)
symbols.def: Uniform density upper bound.

symbols.name: \(L\)
symbols.def: Radius of each anisotropic H\"older ball.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal A\)
symbols.def: Treatment-arm index set.

symbols.name: \(a\)
symbols.def: Treatment-arm index.

symbols.name: \(e\)
symbols.def: Evaluation-fold index; the other fold is the pilot fold.

symbols.name: \(I_{a,e}\)
symbols.def: Deterministic fold \(e\) in arm \(a\), of cardinality \(m\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal Y\)
symbols.def: Scalar outcome support.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal Z_d\)
symbols.def: Covariate support for \(d\ge1\); for \(d=0\), \(\mathcal Z_0\) is a singleton.

symbols.name: \(y\)
symbols.def: Outcome argument.

symbols.name: \(z\)
symbols.def: Covariate argument.

symbols.name: \(h\)
symbols.def: Generic discrepancy direction with zero integral in the outcome coordinate at every covariate value.

symbols.name: \(b\)
symbols.def: Generic bounded covariate amplitude in the cosine second-variation calculation.

symbols.name: \(P_{a,n}\)
symbols.def: Law of the observed outcome and covariate in arm \(a\) at index \(n\).

symbols.name: \(Y_n(a)\)
symbols.def: Potential outcome under arm \(a\), with marginal law induced by \(P_{a,n}\).

symbols.name: \(Y_{a,i,n}\)
symbols.def: Outcome coordinate of observation \(i\) in arm \(a\).

symbols.name: \(Z_{a,i,n}\)
symbols.def: Covariate coordinate of observation \(i\) in arm \(a\).

symbols.name: \(W_{a,i,n}\)
symbols.def: Observation \(W_{a,i,n}=(Y_{a,i,n},Z_{a,i,n})\) from arm \(a\).

symbols.name: \(R_n\)
symbols.def: Common covariate marginal of the two arm laws.

symbols.name: \(r_n\)
symbols.def: Lebesgue density of \(R_n\) for \(d\ge1\), and the constant one for \(d=0\).

symbols.name: \(Q_{a,n}\)
symbols.def: Conditional law of the outcome given the covariate in arm \(a\).

symbols.name: \(q_{a,n}\)
symbols.def: Conditional density defined by \(Q_{a,n}(dy\mid z)=q_{a,n}(y,z)dy\).

symbols.name: \(\bar q_n\)
symbols.def: Reference density \(\bar q_n=(q_{0,n}+q_{1,n})/2\).

symbols.name: \(\Delta_n\)
symbols.def: Conditional-law discrepancy \(\Delta_n=q_{1,n}-q_{0,n}\), which integrates to zero in \(y\) at every \(z\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal G_{n,z}\)
symbols.def: Weighted Neumann inverse: \(u=\mathcal G_{n,z}h\) solves \(-\partial_y(\bar q_n(y,z)\partial_yu(y))=h(y)\), \(\partial_yu(0)=\partial_yu(1)=0\), and \(\int_0^1u(y)dy=0\).

symbols.name: \(\rho_n\)
symbols.def: Inverse-elliptic separation defined by \(\rho_n^2=\int\Delta_n(y,z)(\mathcal G_{n,z}\Delta_n(\cdot,z))(y)dydR_n(z)\).

symbols.name: \(\rho\)
symbols.def: Radius of a local neighborhood of conditional equality.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\)
symbols.def: Local anisotropic conditional-transport model class declared in the definitions array.

symbols.name: \(\theta_n\)
symbols.def: Conditional quadratic transport endpoint \(\theta_n=\int_{\mathcal Z_d}W_2^2(Q_{0,n}(\cdot\mid z),Q_{1,n}(\cdot\mid z))dR_n(z)\), the sharp lower endpoint of \(E[(Y_n(1)-Y_n(0))^2]\) over conditional couplings.

symbols.name: \(\Psi_y\)
symbols.def: Compactly supported boundary-corrected outcome wavelets, with the constant removed from discrepancy projections.

symbols.name: \(\Psi_z\)
symbols.def: Tensor boundary-corrected covariate wavelets when \(d\ge1\), and the singleton constant basis when \(d=0\).

symbols.name: \(J_y\)
symbols.def: Outcome resolution.

symbols.name: \(J_z\)
symbols.def: Covariate resolution, used only when \(d\ge1\).

symbols.name: \(J_y^*\)
symbols.def: Rate-balancing outcome resolution for the conditional branch.

symbols.name: \(J_z^*\)
symbols.def: Rate-balancing covariate resolution for the conditional branch.

symbols.name: \(J_y^0\)
symbols.def: Growing outcome resolution for the no-covariate branch.

symbols.name: \(\bar J_y\)
symbols.def: Outcome resolution of each opposite-fold pilot density estimator.

symbols.name: \(\bar J_z\)
symbols.def: Covariate resolution of each opposite-fold pilot density estimator.

symbols.name: \(\beta\)
symbols.def: Effective anisotropic pilot smoothness defined by \(\beta^{-1}=s_y^{-1}+d s_z^{-1}\) for \(d\ge1\).

symbols.name: \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\)
symbols.def: Uniform pilot scale \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}=(\log n/n)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}\).

symbols.name: \(\lambda_n\)
symbols.def: Galerkin ridge satisfying \(\lambda_n=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\downarrow0\).

symbols.name: \(T\)
symbols.def: Fixed clipping map \(T(x)=\min\{2C,\max\{c/2,x\}\}\).

symbols.name: \(\Lambda_{J_y,J_z}^{(d)}\)
symbols.def: Indices of tensor products of nonconstant outcome wavelets through \(J_y\) and covariate wavelets through \(J_z\); for \(d=0\), only the singleton covariate index is retained.

symbols.name: \(\Phi_{J_y,J_z}\)
symbols.def: Column vector \(\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)=(\psi^y_\lambda(y)\psi^z_\gamma(z))_{(\lambda,\gamma)\in\Lambda_{J_y,J_z}^{(d)}}\).

symbols.name: \(D_{J_y,J_z}\)
symbols.def: Projection dimension \(D_{J_y,J_z}=|\Lambda_{J_y,J_z}^{(d)}|\asymp2^{J_y+dJ_z}\).

symbols.name: \(\Pi_{J_y,J_z}\)
symbols.def: Orthogonal projection in \(L^2(dy\,dR_n)\) onto the declared anisotropic tensor features.

symbols.name: \(P_{J_y}\)
symbols.def: Orthogonal outcome-wavelet projector onto the zero-mean levels through \(J_y\).

symbols.name: \(H_y^{-1}\)
symbols.def: Outcome-wavelet negative-order reference with coefficient weight \(2^{-2j_y}\) at outcome level \(j_y\), tensored with the identity over retained covariate coordinates.

symbols.name: \(\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Projected discrepancy coefficients \(\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)\Delta_n(y,z)dydR_n(z)\).

symbols.name: \(\Gamma_{a,J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Arm covariance \(\Gamma_{a,J_y,J_z,n}=\operatorname{Cov}_{P_{a,n}}\{\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,1,n})\}\).

symbols.name: \(\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Two-sample covariance \(\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{0,J_y,J_z,n}+\Gamma_{1,J_y,J_z,n}\), the covariance of a foldwise contrast multiplied by \(\sqrt m\).

symbols.name: \(u\)
symbols.def: Positive threshold for the spectral counting function.

symbols.name: \(\xi_{e,k}\)
symbols.def: Independent standard Gaussian coordinates indexed by fold and Hessian eigenvector.

symbols.name: \(\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Boundary-wavelet projection of the arm \(a\) joint density at resolutions \((\bar J_y,\bar J_z)\), computed only from pilot fold \(I_{a,3-e}\).

symbols.name: \(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Average of the two armwise covariate-marginal wavelet projections from the opposite folds.

symbols.name: \(\widehat r_n^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Normalized clipping of \(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}\) to fixed positive bounds.

symbols.name: \(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Raw ratio \(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}=\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}/\widehat r_n^{(-e)}\), defined everywhere because the marginal pilot is positive.

symbols.name: \(\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Conditionally normalized clipping of \(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) to fixed positive bounds.

symbols.name: \(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Pilot reference density \(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}=(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}+\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)})/2\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal E_n^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Clipping-inactive event on which both normalized raw conditional pilots and the raw marginal pilot lie strictly inside their clipping bounds.

symbols.name: \(\widehat f_n^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Pilot conditional transport value at each covariate, computed from the two densities \(\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Observable one-dimensional Kantorovich derivative of \(\widehat f_n^{(-e)}\) with respect to arm \(a\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Pilot plug-in endpoint \(\int\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Sum of the two opposite-fold empirical covariance matrices of \(\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Observed opposite-fold first-order score for arm \(a\), including one half of the shared-marginal value score and the centered conditional Kantorovich potential.

symbols.name: \(\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Pilot feature mean \(\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dydz\).

symbols.name: \(X_{a,i}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Centered evaluation-fold feature \(X_{a,i}^{(-e)}=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})-\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Equal-weight two-fold cross-fitted anisotropic second-order estimator for the \(d\ge1\) branch.

symbols.name: \(\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Foldwise second-order value evaluated on fold \(e\) using the opposite fold as pilot.

symbols.name: \(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: First Hoeffding projection of \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n\).

symbols.name: \(\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Canonical diagonal-free second Hoeffding projection of \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n\).

symbols.name: \(V_{L,n}\)
symbols.def: Linear variance constant \(V_{L,n}=n\operatorname{Var}(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n})\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat V_{L,n}\)
symbols.def: Average across the two folds of the sum of the two within-arm sample variances of \(\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}\).

symbols.name: \(B^y_{J_y,n}\)
symbols.def: Outcome-frequency truncation bias.

symbols.name: \(B^z_{J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Covariate-frequency truncation bias for \(d\ge1\).

symbols.name: \(r_{n,d}(s_z)\)
symbols.def: Degenerate quadratic estimation scale \(r_{n,d}(s_z)=n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\) for \(d\ge1\), and \(r_{n,0}=n^{-1}\) for \(d=0\).

symbols.name: \(\rho_{Q,n}\)
symbols.def: Zero-to-quadratic transition radius \(\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)}\) for \(d\ge1\), and \(n^{-1/2}\) for \(d=0\).

symbols.name: \(\rho_{L,n}\)
symbols.def: Quadratic-to-linear transition radius \(\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/(2(4s_z+d))}\) for \(d\ge1\), and \(n^{-1/2}\) for \(d=0\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\)
symbols.def: Local minimax root-mean-square scale derived in Theorems 3 and 4.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal K_{J_z}\)
symbols.def: A maximal set of interior covariate wavelets at level \(J_z\) with pairwise disjoint supports; \(M_{J_z}=|\mathcal K_{J_z}|\asymp2^{dJ_z}\).

symbols.name: \(M_{J_z}\)
symbols.def: Cardinality \(M_{J_z}=|\mathcal K_{J_z}|\asymp2^{dJ_z}\).

symbols.name: \(c_0\)
symbols.def: A fixed sufficiently small amplitude constant for the lower-bound families.

symbols.name: \(C_{\chi}\)
symbols.def: Fixed constant in the product-mixture chi-square bound.

symbols.name: \(\omega\)
symbols.def: Rademacher sign vector indexed by \(\mathcal K_{J_z}\).

symbols.name: \(\gamma_n\)
symbols.def: Lower-bound amplitude \(\gamma_n=c_0\min\{2^{-J_z(s_z+d/2)},\rho M_{J_z}^{-1/2}\}\), where \(c_0>0\) is a sufficiently small fixed constant.

symbols.name: \(b_{n,\omega}\)
symbols.def: Sign-paired wavelet amplitude \(b_{n,\omega}(z)=\gamma_n\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_{J_z}}\omega_k\psi^z_{J_z,k}(z)\).

symbols.name: \(q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}\)
symbols.def: Lower-bound conditional densities \(q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}(y,z)=1+(2a-1)b_{n,\omega}(z)\cos(2\pi y)/2\).

symbols.name: \(\overline{\mathbb P}_n\)
symbols.def: Uniform Rademacher mixture of the two-arm product laws induced by \(q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathbb P_n^0\)
symbols.def: Two-arm product law with both conditional densities equal to one.

symbols.name: \(t\)
symbols.def: Fixed-frequency amplitude for the no-covariate submodel.

symbols.name: \(q_{a,t}^{0}\)
symbols.def: No-covariate fixed-frequency density \(q_{a,t}^{0}(y)=1+(2a-1)t\cos(2\pi y)/2\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\theta^0_{J_y,n}\)
symbols.def: Full-sample no-covariate projected empirical-quantile estimator retaining its diagonal term.

symbols.name: \(\mathbb B\)
symbols.def: Standard Brownian bridge.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{mix}}\)
symbols.def: Confidence interval returned by the mixed linear--quadratic calibration handle.

symbols.name: \(C_B\)
symbols.def: Uniform constant multiplying the anisotropic truncation-bias envelope.

symbols.name: \(\mathsf{STAR}\)
symbols.def: Student Achievement and Retention randomized experiment used by Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn to illustrate conditional-transport causal bounds.

symbols.name: \(a_y\)
symbols.def: Effective outcome H\"older modulus exponent \(a_y=\min\{s_y,1\}\).

symbols.name: \(K_n\)
symbols.def: Number of independent blocks in the supplemental median direct-COT estimator, chosen so that \(K_n\asymp\log n\).

symbols.name: \(J_y^{\mathrm{op}}\)
symbols.def: Oversampled outcome resolution for the ridge Galerkin solve, chosen minimally so that \(J_y^{\mathrm{op}}\ge J_y\) and \(2^{-2J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Ridge Galerkin inverse of the pilot weighted Neumann operator on the oversampled zero-outcome-mean space through \(J_y^{\mathrm{op}}\).

symbols.name: \(N_n\)
symbols.def: Block size \(N_n=\lfloor n/K_n\rfloor\) in the supplemental median direct-COT estimator.

symbols.name: \(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm{dir,med}}\)
symbols.def: Median of the \(K_n\) blockwise direct conditional-optimal-transport values in the observable pilot-feasibility proposition.

symbols.name: \(G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Finite common-marginal Gram matrix \(G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}\Phi_{J_y,J_z}^{\top}dy\,dR_n\).

symbols.name: \(H^{\mathrm{form}}_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Coefficient matrix of the projected inverse-elliptic bilinear form before conversion to raw feature-moment coordinates.

symbols.name: \(B_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Raw feature-moment Hessian \(B_{J_y,J_z,n}=G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}H^{\mathrm{form}}_{J_y,J_z,n}G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}\).

symbols.name: \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: One-fold whitened raw-moment Hessian \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}B_{J_y,J_z,n}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathsf K_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Normalized two-fold Hessian \(\mathsf K_{J_y,J_z,n}=K_{J_y,J_z,n}\oplus K_{J_y,J_z,n}\), because \(n(\widehat\theta-\theta)=m\sum_{e=1}^2(\widehat\theta_e-\theta)\) for the equal-weight two-fold estimator.

symbols.name: \(\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Nonzero eigenvalues of \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}\), repeated with multiplicity.

symbols.name: \(N_{J_y,J_z,n}(u)\)
symbols.def: Counting function \(N_{J_y,J_z,n}(u)=|\{k:\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\ge u\}|\) of the globally ordered one-fold spectrum.

symbols.name: \(v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Orthonormal eigenvectors of \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}\) corresponding to \(\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\).

symbols.name: \(\eta_{k,n}\)
symbols.def: Whitened local shift \(\eta_{k,n}=v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt{m}\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}=2^{-1/2}v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt n\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}\).

symbols.name: \(A_{J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Two-fold null standard-deviation constant \(A_{J_y,J_z,n}=\{2\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\}^{1/2}=2\|K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\).

symbols.name: \(S_n\)
symbols.def: Triangular normalization \(S_n=A_{J_y,J_z,n}+\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Opposite-fold Gram matrix obtained by integrating \(\Phi_{J_y,J_z}\Phi_{J_y,J_z}^{\top}\) against \(dy\,\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat H_{\mathrm{form},J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Observed opposite-fold inverse-elliptic bilinear-form matrix before Gram conjugation.

symbols.name: \(\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Observed raw-moment Hessian \(\widehat B=(\widehat G_{R,J})^{-1}\widehat H_{\mathrm{form}}(\widehat G_{R,J})^{-1}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\)
symbols.def: Observable whitened raw-moment Hessian \((\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n}\)
symbols.def: Diagonal-free within-arm plus cross-arm quadratic correction using the observed raw-moment Hessian \(\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\).

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\), the observations \(W_{a,1,n},\ldots,W_{a,n,n}\) are i.i.d. from \(P_{a,n}\) within each \(a\in\mathcal A\), and the two arm samples are independent.
The \(\mathcal Z_d\)-marginal of \(P_{a,n}\) equals \(R_n\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).
For \(d\ge1\), the common marginal density satisfies \(c\le r_n(z)\le C\) for every \(z\in\mathcal Z_d\).
The conditional densities satisfy \(c\le q_{a,n}(y,z)\le C\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \((y,z)\in\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z_d\).
Each \(q_{a,n}\) belongs to the tensor anisotropic ball \(\mathcal C^{s_y,s_z}(\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z_d;L)\), with the \(z\)-condition omitted when \(d=0\).
The bases \(\Psi_y\) and \(\Psi_z\) are compactly supported boundary wavelets with regularities strictly greater than \(s_y+1\) and \(s_z\), respectively.
The H\"older radius satisfies \(L>1\), so the uniform density is an interior point of the declared H\"older balls.

definitions.name: Local anisotropic conditional-transport class \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\)
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}):\text{the declared sampling, common-marginal, density-bound, anisotropic-smoothness, and local-radius properties hold at indices }(n,d)\}.\]

definitions.name: Anisotropic conditional projection
definitions.construction:
Let
\[
G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}=\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}
\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)^{\top}\,dy\,dR_n(z).
\]
For \(d\ge1\), define the \(L^2(dy\,dR_n)\)-orthogonal projection by
\[
\Pi_{J_y,J_z}h
=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}^{\top}G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}
\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)h(y,z)\,dy\,dR_n(z).
\]
For \(d=0\), \(G_{R,J_y,0,n}=I\) and the same formula retains only the outcome-wavelet sum through \(J_y\).

definitions.name: Two-sample covariance whitening and normalized Hessian
definitions.construction:
Let \(G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}\) be the Gram matrix in the anisotropic-projection definition and form the inverse-elliptic bilinear-form matrix
\[
H^{\mathrm{form}}_{J_y,J_z,n;\lambda\mu}
=\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}\Phi_\lambda(y,z)
\{\mathcal G_{n,z}\Phi_\mu(\cdot,z)\}(y)\,dy\,dR_n(z).
\]
The Hessian in raw feature-moment coordinates is
\[
B_{J_y,J_z,n}=G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}H^{\mathrm{form}}_{J_y,J_z,n}G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}.
\]
Form \(\Gamma_{a,J_y,J_z,n}=\operatorname{Cov}_{P_{a,n}}\{\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,1,n})\}\), \(\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{0,J_y,J_z,n}+\Gamma_{1,J_y,J_z,n}\),
\[
K_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}B_{J_y,J_z,n}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2},
\qquad
\mathsf K_{J_y,J_z,n}=K_{J_y,J_z,n}\oplus K_{J_y,J_z,n}.
\]
Let \((\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n},v_{k,J_y,J_z,n})\) be the eigenpairs of the one-fold matrix, set
\[
\eta_{k,n}=v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt{n/2}\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n},
\qquad
A_{J_y,J_z,n}=\left\{4\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\right\}^{1/2}.
\]

definitions.name: Observable equal-weight two-fold anisotropic second-order estimator
definitions.construction:
Partition each arm into deterministic folds \(I_{a,1}\) and \(I_{a,2}\), each of size \(m=n/2\). On pilot fold \(3-e\), let \(\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be the empirical boundary-wavelet joint-density projection through \((\bar J_y,\bar J_z)\), and set \(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z)=\frac12\sum_{a=0}^1\int_0^1\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du\). With \(T(x)=\min\{2C,\max\{c/2,x\}\}\), define \(\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)=T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z))/\int T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(v))dv\), \(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)/\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)\), and \(\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z))/\int_0^1T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z))du\). The event \(\mathcal E_n^{(-e)}\) is \(c/2<\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}<2C\) and \(c/2<\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}<2C\) pointwise for both arms; clipping is inactive on this event, while normalization enforces exact conditional mass. The displayed operations keep every object defined on its complement. Put \(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}=(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}+\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)})/2\) and, on the oversampled zero-outcome-mean wavelet space through \(J_y^{\mathrm{op}}\), set
\[
\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}=
\left[P_{J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}\{-\partial_y(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)\partial_y)\}P_{J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}+\lambda_n I\right]^{-1}P_{J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}
=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)^{\top}\,dy\,\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz,
\]
\[
\widehat H_{\mathrm{form},J_y,J_z,n;\lambda\mu}^{(-e)}
=\int\Phi_\lambda(y,z)\{\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}\Phi_\mu(\cdot,z)\}(y)\,dy\,\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz,
\]
and the raw-moment-coordinate Hessian
\[
\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}
=\{\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\}^{-1}
\widehat H_{\mathrm{form},J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}
\{\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\}^{-1}.
\]
Let \(\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)=W_2^2(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy,\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy)\), let \(\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be its observable one-dimensional Kantorovich derivative in arm \(a\), and let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}=\int\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz\). The explicit first-order score is
\[
\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\frac12\{\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)-\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}\}+\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)-\int_0^1\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du.
\]
Set \(X_{a,i}^{(-e)}=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})-\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\), where \(\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\widehat r_n^{(-e)}\). The diagonal-free correction in raw moment coordinates is
\[
\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\frac{1}{m(m-1)}\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{i\ne j\in I_{a,e}}(X_{a,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{a,j}^{(-e)}-\frac{2}{m^2}\sum_{i\in I_{1,e}}\sum_{j\in I_{0,e}}(X_{1,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{0,j}^{(-e)}.
\]
Finally,
\[
\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}+\sum_{a=0}^1\frac1m\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})+\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n},
\qquad
\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}.
\]

definitions.name: Pilot resolutions, ridge, and observable linear variance
definitions.construction:
For \(d\ge1\), set \(\beta^{-1}=s_y^{-1}+ds_z^{-1}\), \(2^{\bar J_y}\asymp(n/\log n)^{\beta/(s_y(2\beta+1))}\), \(2^{\bar J_z}\asymp(n/\log n)^{\beta/(s_z(2\beta+1))}\), \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}=(\log n/n)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}\), and \(\lambda_n=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\). For each point-estimator outcome resolution, let \(J_y^{\mathrm{op}}\ge J_y\) be the smallest integer satisfying \(2^{-2J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\). Let \(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\) be the sum over \(a=0,1\) of the usual sample covariance of \(\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})\), \(i\in I_{a,3-e}\), and set
\[
\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}.
\]
If \(\bar s_{a,e}=m^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})\), define
\[
V_{L,n}=n\operatorname{Var}(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}),
\qquad
\widehat V_{L,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_{a=0}^1\frac{1}{m-1}\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\{\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})-\bar s_{a,e}\}^2.
\]

definitions.name: Conditional smoothness--separation rate
definitions.construction: For \(d\ge1\), define \(\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\}\), where \(r_{n,d}(s_z)=n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\). The zero-to-quadratic boundary is \(\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)}\), and the quadratic-to-linear boundary is \(\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/(2(4s_z+d))}\).

definitions.name: No-covariate growing-outcome-resolution branch
definitions.construction:
When \(d=0\), define the empirical distribution function in arm \(a\) by \(\widehat F_{a,n}(y)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{Y_{a,i,n}\le y\}\) and its left-continuous generalized inverse by \(\widehat Q_{a,n}(u)=\inf\{y\in[0,1]:\widehat F_{a,n}(y)\ge u\}\). Let \(V^Q_{J_y}\) be the span of all boundary scaling functions and wavelets from \(\Psi_y\) through level \(J_y\), with the constant scaling function retained, and let \(P^Q_{J_y}\) be the \(L^2[0,1]\)-orthogonal projector onto \(V^Q_{J_y}\). Define the full-sample statistic
\[
\widehat\theta^0_{J_y,n}=\int_0^1\left[P^Q_{J_y}\{\widehat Q_{1,n}-\widehat Q_{0,n}\}(u)\right]^2du .
\]
Choose \(J_y^0\) so that \(2^{J_y^0}\to\infty\), \(2^{J_y^0}=o(n)\), and \(2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y^0}=o(n^{-1})\). The square retains its diagonal term. Define \(\mathfrak R_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\}\).

definitions.name: Sign-paired conditional wavelet family
definitions.construction: For \(d\ge1\), set \(2^{J_z}\asymp n^{2/(4s_z+d)}\), \(b_{n,\omega}=\gamma_n\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_{J_z}}\omega_k\psi^z_{J_z,k}\), \(r_n(z)=1\), and \(q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}(y,z)=1+(2a-1)b_{n,\omega}(z)\cos(2\pi y)/2\). The null member has \(b_{n,\omega}=0\).

definitions.name: Fixed-frequency no-covariate family
definitions.construction: For \(d=0\), set \(q_{a,t}^{0}(y)=1+(2a-1)t\cos(2\pi y)/2\); use the pairs \(t=0\) and \(t=c_0n^{-1/2}\) at equality, and \(t=t_0\) and \(t=t_0+c_0n^{-1/2}\) for a fixed sufficiently small \(t_0\ne0\).

definitions.name: Mixed linear--quadratic calibration handle
definitions.construction: Use the displayed cross-fitted scores \(\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}\), raw-moment-coordinate Hessians \(\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\), and diagonal-free kernels \(\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n}\). Any future calibration must apply common Gaussian multipliers to the linear and quadratic summands while retaining their covariance and must enlarge the inverted two-sided critical region by the deterministic envelope \(C_B\{2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+\mathbf 1\{d\ge1\}2^{-2s_zJ_z}\}\). The intended target object is \(\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{mix}}\), with no pretest or variance-threshold switch; this handle does not itself define a multiplier statistic, a critical value, or a confidence interval.

statements.statement: For \(q_{0,n}(y,z)=1-b(z)\cos(2\pi y)/2\) and \(q_{1,n}(y,z)=1+b(z)\cos(2\pi y)/2\), uniformly as \(\|b\|_{\infty}\to0\), \[\theta_n=\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{\mathcal Z_d}b(z)^2dR_n(z)+O(\|b\|_{\infty}^3),\qquad D\theta_n|_{q_{0,n}=q_{1,n}}=0,\qquad \frac12D^2\theta_n[h,h]=\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}h(y,z)(\mathcal G_{n,z}h(\cdot,z))(y)dydR_n(z).\] In particular, the scalar path \(q_{0,n}=1\), \(q_{1,n}=1+t b(z)\cos(2\pi y)\) has second derivative \((4\pi^2)^{-1}\int b^2dR_n\) at \(t=0\).
statements.justification: The exact coefficient fixes the Hessian convention, the lower-bound separation, and the null-law constants.
statements.gap: LinGaoBlanchetGlynn2026SmoothCOT stops at a vanishing first derivative, while GoldmanHuesmannOtto2021 supplies deterministic Poisson linearization but not this conditional statistical second variation.
statements.consumer: The sign-paired lower-bound family and the \(\mathsf{STAR}\) simulation benchmark use this coefficient.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(z\) and let \(q(\cdot,z)\) be a common conditional density with \(c\le q\le C\).  For a direction \(h(\cdot,z)\) satisfying \(\int_0^1h(y,z)dy=0\), define
\[
H_h(y,z)=\int_0^y h(x,z)dx .
\]
Then \(H_h(0,z)=H_h(1,z)=0\).  Consider the symmetric path \(q_{0,t}=q-th/2\), \(q_{1,t}=q+th/2\), for \(|t|\) small enough that both densities stay positive.  If \(F_{a,t}\) and \(Q_{a,t}=F_{a,t}^{-1}\) are the corresponding distribution and quantile functions, differentiation of \(F_{a,t}\{Q_{a,t}(u,z),z\}=u\), justified by \(q_{a,t}\ge c/2\), gives
\[
\dot Q_{1,0}(u,z)-\dot Q_{0,0}(u,z)
=-\frac{H_h(Q(u,z),z)}{q(Q(u,z),z)}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
At \(t=0\) the two quantiles coincide.  Hence the first derivative of their squared \(L^2(0,1)\) distance is zero, and differentiating a second time gives
\[
\frac12D^2W_2^2(q\,dy,q\,dy)[h,h]
=\int_0^1\{\dot Q_{1,0}(u,z)-\dot Q_{0,0}(u,z)\}^2du.
\]
Changing variables \(u=F(y,z)\) in this display and using (1) yields
\[
\frac12D^2W_2^2(q\,dy,q\,dy)[h,h]
=\int_0^1\frac{H_h(y,z)^2}{q(y,z)}dy.                                      \tag{2}
\]
Let \(u_h=\mathcal G_{n,z}h\).  Integrating the defining equation
\(-\partial_y(q\partial_yu_h)=h\) from \(0\) to \(y\), and using the Neumann boundary condition at zero, gives
\[
q(y,z)\partial_yu_h(y,z)=-H_h(y,z).
\]
Integration by parts has no boundary term because \(H_h(0,z)=H_h(1,z)=0\), and therefore
\[
\int_0^1h(y,z)u_h(y,z)dy
=\int_0^1q(y,z)|\partial_yu_h(y,z)|^2dy
=\int_0^1\frac{H_h(y,z)^2}{q(y,z)}dy.                                      \tag{3}
\]
Equations (2)--(3), integrated with respect to the common marginal \(R_n\), prove the asserted vanishing first derivative and inverse-elliptic second variation.  The common marginal is supplied by \(\mathrm{ass{:}shared\text{-}covariate\text{-}marginal}\), and every division above is licensed by \(\mathrm{ass{:}conditional\text{-}density\text{-}bounds}\).

For the displayed cosine pair, put \(e=b(z)/2\).  The two conditional distribution functions are
\[
F_{1,e}(y)=y+\frac{e}{2\pi}\sin(2\pi y),\qquad
F_{0,e}(y)=y-\frac{e}{2\pi}\sin(2\pi y).
\]
For \(|e|<1\), their derivatives are uniformly bounded away from zero.  Taylor expansion of the inverse identities, with the remainder controlled uniformly by that lower derivative bound, gives
\[
F_{1,e}^{-1}(u)-F_{0,e}^{-1}(u)
=-\frac{2e}{2\pi}\sin(2\pi u)+O(|e|^2)
=-\frac{b(z)}{2\pi}\sin(2\pi u)+O(|b(z)|^2).                              \tag{4}
\]
Squaring (4), integrating over \(u\), and using \(\int_0^1\sin^2(2\pi u)du=1/2\) proves
\[
W_2^2(Q_{0,n}(\cdot\mid z),Q_{1,n}(\cdot\mid z))
=\frac{b(z)^2}{8\pi^2}+O(|b(z)|^3).                                        \tag{5}
\]
Since \(R_n\) is a probability measure, its integral remainder is \(O(\|b\|_\infty^3)\).  Finally, on the one-sided path \(q_0=1\), \(q_1=1+t b(z)\cos(2\pi y)\), equation (2) applies with \(H_h=b(z)\sin(2\pi y)/(2\pi)\).  Thus the coefficient of \(t^2\) is \(\int b^2dR_n/(8\pi^2)\), and the second derivative is \(\int b^2dR_n/(4\pi^2)\), as claimed.

statements.statement:
Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,ho)\), there are fixed constants \(0<c_H<C_H<\infty\) and \(0<c_\Gamma<C_\Gamma<\infty\) such that, if \(g=\sum_{(j_y,k_y,\gamma)\in\Lambda_{J_y,J_z}^{(d)}}x_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}\psi^y_{j_y,k_y}\psi^z_\gamma\), then \[c_H\sum_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}2^{-2j_y}x_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}^2\le\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}g(y,z)\{\mathcal G_{n,z}g(\cdot,z)\}(y)dydR_n(z)\le C_H\sum_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}2^{-2j_y}x_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}^2,\] and \(c_\Gamma I\preceq\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}\preceq C_\Gamma I\). The min--max principle therefore transfers the globally ordered spectrum of the diagonal \(H_y^{-1}\) reference to \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}\): for \(2^{-2J_y}\le u\le1\) and \(1\le k\le D_{J_y,J_z}\), \[N_{J_y,J_z,n}(u)\asymp\min\{D_{J_y,J_z},2^{dJ_z}u^{-1/2}\},\qquad 
u_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\asymp\min\{1,(2^{dJ_z}/k)^2\}.\] Consequently, for \(d\ge1\), \[\|K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\asymp1,\qquad \|K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\asymp2^{dJ_z},\qquad  rac{\max_k|
u_{k,J_y,J_z,n}|}{\{\sum_k
u_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\}^{1/2}}\lesssim2^{-dJ_z/2}.\] The same quadratic-form comparison and anisotropic approximation give \( |B^y_{J_y,n}|\lesssim2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}\) and \( |B^z_{J_z,n}|\lesssim2^{-2s_zJ_z}\). When \(d=0\), the Hilbert--Schmidt norm remains bounded above and away from zero as \(J_y	o\infty\).
statements.justification: The min--max argument makes the spectrum canonical despite variable-coefficient mixing and determines both anisotropic tuning parameters.
statements.gap: NilesWeedBerthet2022 gives negative-order wavelet geometry for unconditional loss, but it does not separate outcome elliptic smoothing from replicated covariate directions in a conditional Hessian.
statements.consumer: The expansion, minimax rate, spectral transition, and confidence bias envelope all use these three scales.

statements.statement:
Let \(d\ge1\) and put \(a_y=\min\{s_y,1\}\). For the opposite-fold estimator and the declared pilot resolutions, uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\max_e\left[\|\widehat r_n^{(-e)}-r_n\|_\infty+\max_a\|\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}-q_{a,n}\|_\infty\right]=O_P(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}),
\qquad
P\left(\bigcap_{e=1}^2\mathcal E_n^{(-e)}\right)\to1.
\]
The clipping is inactive on that event, and conditional normalization is exact everywhere. The fixed density bounds imply
\[
\frac{c}{4C}I\preceq G_{R,J_y,J_z,n},\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\preceq\frac{4C}{c}I
\]
for every fold and every realization. Moreover,
\[
\max_e\left[
\|\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|\{\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\}^{-1}-G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-B_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\right]
=O_P(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{a_y}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}+\lambda_n).
\]
The plug-in, Gram, ridge, and operator contribution to the second-order expansion is
\[
O_P\!\left\{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+
\rho_n^{\,2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2\right\}
+o_P(1)\left\{\frac{\rho_n}{\sqrt n}+\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}n\right\}.
\]
Hence it is negligible relative to the displayed expansion scale whenever
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho_n^{\,2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2
=o\!\left(\frac{\rho_n}{\sqrt n}+\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}n+2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}\right).
\]
If additionally \(D_{J_y,J_z}\log n/m=o(1)\), then
\[
\max_e\|\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1),
\qquad
\max_e\|\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1),
\]
and \(\max_e\|\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}=o_P(\|K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{HS}})\). This extra covariance condition is required only when the population triangular proxy is replaced by its observed spectral plug-in, not for the point estimator.
statements.justification: This result separates what the primitive smoothness class actually guarantees for the observable pilots from the stronger covariance condition needed only for a plug-in spectral display.
statements.gap: SmoothCOT Section 3.3 and Appendix C.4 control a first-order wavelet plug-in remainder, but they do not estimate a zero-mean Gram-corrected Galerkin Hessian or quantify clipping, ridge, Gram, and covariance errors for a growing second-order kernel.
statements.consumer: The expansion, minimax theorem, and spectral transition use the Gram and kernel conclusions; an implementable spectral diagnostic additionally uses the final covariance conclusion.

statements.statement:
Assume \(L>1\). For the sign-paired conditional wavelet construction and a sufficiently small fixed \(c_0\), every \(b_{n,\omega}\) has zero conditional mass after multiplication by \(\cos(2\pi y)\), \(q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}\ge c\), anisotropic H\"older norm at most \(L\), common marginal \(R_n(dz)=dz\), and inverse-elliptic radius at most \(\rho\). Its endpoint separation from the null equals
\[
\frac{\gamma_n^2M_{J_z}}{8\pi^2}\{1+o(1)\}.
\]
The uniform Rademacher mixture and the null product law satisfy
\[
\chi^2(\overline{\mathbb P}_n,\mathbb P_n^0)\le\exp\{C_{\chi}n^2\gamma_n^4M_{J_z}\}-1.
\]
At \(2^{J_z}\asymp n^{2/(4s_z+d)}\), the exponent is bounded and the separation is a fixed multiple of \(\min\{\rho^2,r_{n,d}(s_z)\}\). The fixed-frequency no-covariate construction is positive, normalized, H\"older, and has bounded product Hellinger distance for parameter increments of order \(n^{-1/2}\).
statements.justification: The converse is tied to a named finite family with every membership and testing-distance check exposed.
statements.gap: BickelRitov1988 and IngsterSuslina2003 provide quadratic-functional mixture templates, but not a two-arm conditional-density construction preserving a shared marginal and conditional normalization.
statements.consumer: The conditional minimax frontier uses the Rademacher mixture for the quadratic and zero zones, while the no-covariate recovery theorem uses the fixed-frequency branch.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(c_y(y)=\cos(2\pi y)\).  If \(\rho=0\), then \(\gamma_n=0\), the construction equals the null law, and all membership, separation, and divergence assertions follow immediately.  Suppose henceforth that \(\rho>0\).

Boundary-wavelet scaling and the disjointness of the supports in \(\mathcal K_{J_z}\) give constants depending only on the fixed basis such that
\[
\|b_{n,\omega}\|_\infty
\le C_1\gamma_n2^{dJ_z/2}
\le C_1c_0 2^{-s_zJ_z},
\qquad
\|b_{n,\omega}\|_{\mathcal C^{s_z}}
\le C_2\gamma_n2^{(s_z+d/2)J_z}
\le C_2c_0.                                                               \tag{1}
\]
Because \(L>1\), choose \(c_0\) so small that the perturbation H\"older norm is at most \(L-1\).  Shrinking this same fixed constant if necessary ensures
\[
C_1c_0\le2\min\{1-c,C-1\}.
\]
The outcome frequency is fixed, so its \(\mathcal C^{s_y}\) norm is absorbed in the constants.  Hence
\[
c\le1+(2a-1)b_{n,\omega}(z)c_y(y)/2\le C,
\qquad
\|q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}\|_{\mathcal C^{s_y,s_z}}\le L.             \tag{2}
\]
Moreover,
\[
\int_0^1q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}(y,z)dy
=1+\frac{2a-1}{2}b_{n,\omega}(z)\int_0^1c_y(y)dy=1.                       \tag{3}
\]
Thus the conditional laws are normalized.  Taking \(r_n(z)=1\) gives their common marginal and satisfies the marginal density and smoothness conditions.

For this symmetric pair, \(\bar q_n=1\) and \(\Delta_n=b_{n,\omega}c_y\).  The declared Neumann inverse is explicit:
\[
\mathcal G_{n,z}\Delta_n(\cdot,z)
=\frac{b_{n,\omega}(z)}{4\pi^2}c_y.
\]
It has zero integral and zero derivative at both endpoints.  Orthonormality of the selected covariate wavelets gives
\[
\int_{\mathcal Z_d}b_{n,\omega}(z)^2dz
=\gamma_n^2\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_{J_z}}\omega_k^2
=\gamma_n^2M_{J_z}.
\]
Consequently
\[
\rho_n^2
=\frac{\gamma_n^2M_{J_z}}{8\pi^2}
\le\frac{c_0^2}{8\pi^2}\rho^2
\le\rho^2,                                                               \tag{4}
\]
where the penultimate inequality is the radius branch in the definition of \(\gamma_n\), and the last follows from the fixed small choice of \(c_0\).  Equations (1)--(4), together with the sampling construction, prove membership in \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\).

By the cosine second-variation lemma,
\[
\theta_{n,\omega}
=\frac{\gamma_n^2M_{J_z}}{8\pi^2}+O(\|b_{n,\omega}\|_\infty^3).           \tag{5}
\]
Here \(\gamma_n^2M_{J_z}\asymp(\gamma_n2^{dJ_z/2})^2\), whereas (1) makes \(\|b_{n,\omega}\|_\infty=o(1)\).  Therefore the remainder in (5) is \(o(\gamma_n^2M_{J_z})\), uniformly in \(\omega\), proving the asserted endpoint separation.

Under \(\mathbb P_n^0\), let \(L_\omega\) be the likelihood ratio of the two-arm product alternative.  Arm and observation independence, \(\int_0^1c_y^2dy=1/2\), and wavelet orthonormality imply, for sign vectors \(\omega,\omega'\),
\[
E_0(L_\omega L_{\omega'})
=\left\{1+\frac18\int b_{n,\omega}b_{n,\omega'}dz\right\}^{2n}
=\left\{1+\frac{\gamma_n^2}{8}
\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_{J_z}}\omega_k\omega'_k\right\}^{2n}.              \tag{6}
\]
The factor in braces is positive by (2).  Since \(\log(1+x)\le x\) for \(x>-1\), averaging (6) over independent uniform sign vectors and putting \(\epsilon_k=\omega_k\omega'_k\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
1+\chi^2(\overline{\mathbb P}_n,\mathbb P_n^0)
&\le E_\epsilon\exp\left\{\frac{n\gamma_n^2}{4}
\sum_{k=1}^{M_{J_z}}\epsilon_k\right\}\\
&=\{\cosh(n\gamma_n^2/4)\}^{M_{J_z}}
\le\exp\{n^2\gamma_n^4M_{J_z}/32\}.
\end{aligned}                                                             \tag{7}
\]
The last inequality follows from the power series bound \(\cosh x\le e^{x^2/2}\).  Thus the claim holds for every fixed \(C_\chi\ge1/32\).  At \(2^{J_z}\asymp n^{2/(4s_z+d)}\),
\[
n^2\gamma_n^4M_{J_z}
\le Cc_0^4n^2 2^{-(4s_z+d)J_z}=O(c_0^4),
\]
and
\[
\gamma_n^2M_{J_z}
\asymp c_0^2\min\{2^{-2s_zJ_z},\rho^2\}
\asymp c_0^2\min\{r_{n,d}(s_z),\rho^2\}.                                \tag{8}
\]

For the no-covariate family, \(q_{a,t}^0=1+(2a-1)tc_y/2\) integrates to one.  The same \(L>1\) slack and a sufficiently small fixed neighborhood of zero give positivity, the upper density bound, and the H\"older constraint.  If \(|t'-t|\le Cn^{-1/2}\), then positivity and \((\sqrt x-\sqrt y)^2\le(x-y)^2/y\) imply for one observation
\[
H^2(q_{a,t}^0,q_{a,t'}^0)
\le\int_0^1\frac{\{q_{a,t}^0(y)-q_{a,t'}^0(y)\}^2}{q_{a,t'}^0(y)}dy
\le C'(t-t')^2.
\]
For product measures, expanding \(1-\prod_j(1-H_j^2/2)\) bounds the product squared Hellinger distance by the sum of the component distances.  Across the two independent samples this is at most \(2nC'(t-t')^2=O(1)\), which completes the final assertion.

statements.statement:
Let \(d\ge1\), put \(a_y=\min\{s_y,1\}\), let \(J_y,J_z\to\infty\), let \(D_{J_y,J_z}=o(n^2)\), and use the observable anisotropic estimator with the declared pilot tuning and studentizer. If
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho_n^{2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2
=o\!\left(\frac{\rho_n}{\sqrt n}+\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}n+2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}\right),
\]
then, uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n=\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}+\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n}+B^y_{J_y,n}+B^z_{J_z,n}+o_P\!\left(\frac{\rho_n}{\sqrt n}+\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}n+2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}\right).
\]
Here \(\operatorname{sd}(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n})\asymp\rho_n/\sqrt n\), \(\operatorname{sd}(\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n})=A_{J_y,J_z,n}/n\), and \(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}=0\) at conditional equality. At \((J_y^*,J_z^*)\), the three projection and quadratic terms are of order \(r_{n,d}(s_z)\); the observable root-mean-square scale is
\[
\frac{\rho_n}{\sqrt n}+r_{n,d}(s_z)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho_n^{2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2,
\]
and it reduces to \(\rho_n/\sqrt n+r_{n,d}(s_z)\) when the final two terms are of no larger order. No covariance estimate enters this point-estimator expansion.
statements.justification: The uniform expansion is the analytic bridge linking primitive density smoothness and corrected Gram coordinates to the local linear and growing-rank quadratic experiment.
statements.gap: The cited first-order and deterministic transport results do not supply this observable Gram-corrected, ridge-Galerkin, anisotropic second-order expansion with the Holder-valid remainder.
statements.consumer: The spectral law, minimax bracket, and unresolved mixed calibration all use this decomposition.

statements.statement:
Under the uniform second-order expansion, suppose additionally that \(\|\Delta_n\|_\infty\to0\) and
\[
2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}=O(S_n/n),
\qquad
S_n=A_{J_y,J_z,n}+\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}.
\]
Then the finite-\(n\) Gaussian-quadratic proxy based on the corrected raw-moment kernel satisfies
\[
d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
\mathcal L\left[\frac{n\{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n-B^y_{J_y,n}-B^z_{J_z,n}\}}{S_n}\right],
\mathcal L\left[\frac1{S_n}\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}
\{(\xi_{e,k}+\eta_{k,n})^2-(1+\eta_{k,n}^2)\}\right]
\right)\to0,
\]
where \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}B_{J_y,J_z,n}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}\), the spectrum is repeated twice,
\[
A_{J_y,J_z,n}^2=4\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2,
\qquad
\eta_{k,n}=2^{-1/2}v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt n\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}.
\]
The same proxy and the normalized estimator are diffuse locally Gaussian:
\[
d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
\mathcal L\left[\frac{n\{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n-B^y_{J_y,n}-B^z_{J_z,n}\}}{S_n}\right],
\mathcal N\!\left(0,\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}^2+nV_{L,n}}{S_n^2}\right)
\right)\to0.
\]
In particular, at equality all shifts and the linear projection vanish and
\[
\frac{n\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n}}{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
If \(D_{J_y,J_z}\log n/m=o(1)\), the population kernel in the finite-\(n\) proxy may be replaced by the average observed kernel formed from \(\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\). Separately, at fixed unequal laws, if \(\widehat V_{L,n}/V_{L,n}\to_P1\), \(\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}/A_{J_y,J_z,n}\to\infty\), and the displayed bias and remainder are \(o(\sqrt{V_{L,n}/n})\), then
\[
\frac{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n}{\sqrt{\widehat V_{L,n}/n}}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
No fixed or subsequential non-Gaussian chaos is asserted in this growing-covariate-resolution regime.
statements.justification: The theorem makes the corrected finite-sample Gaussian-quadratic proxy primary and proves forced diffuse local Gaussianization with the exact split constants.
statements.gap: SmoothCOT gives a regular central limit theorem and a rate statement at equality; the other comparators do not derive this corrected conditional growing-kernel proxy from primitive smoothness.
statements.consumer: The result determines the local Gaussian scale and the finite-sample proxy that a future honest calibration theorem would need.

statements.statement:
Assume \(L>1\), and put \(a_y=\min\{s_y,1\}\). For every \(d\ge1\), there are constants \(0<c_1<C_1<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class constants, such that
\[
c_1\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\le\inf_{\widetilde\theta_n}\sup_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}\{E(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}
\]
\[
\le C_1\min\!\left[\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2\right],
\]
where \(\mathfrak R_{n,d}=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\}\). The observable upper bound uses \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y^*,J_z^*,n}\), or the zero estimator when \(\rho\lesssim\rho_{Q,n}\). The quadratic and zero-zone lower bounds hold on the explicit sign-paired family in the mixture-check lemma. In the zone \(\rho\gg n^{-1/2}\), extending \(q_{a,t}^{0}\) constantly in \(z\) and comparing \(t=c_0\rho\) with \(t=c_0\rho+c_0n^{-1/2}\) supplies the regular \(\rho n^{-1/2}\) lower bound. The bracket is matched whenever
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2
=O\{\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\}.
\]
In this matching region the intrinsic quadratic elbow is \(s_z=d/4\): when \(s_z>d/4\), \(\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)}\) and \(\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/(2(4s_z+d))}\) delimit zero, quadratic, mixed, and regular zones; when \(s_z\le d/4\), the quadratic term prevents a positive-variance root-\(n\) rate uniformly over the class. Outside the matching region, the displayed two-sided bracket is the conclusion and its tightness is not asserted.
statements.justification: The theorem recomputes the elbow from the corrected raw-moment spectrum, exposes the observable pilot restriction, and matches the feasible region with an explicit converse.
statements.gap: The comparator results do not state this equality-local minimax frontier or its Holder-order observable bracket.
statements.consumer: Analysts can distinguish the intrinsic covariate-smoothness obstruction from the stronger smoothness required by the present observable pilot construction.

statements.statement:
Assume \(L>1\). When \(d=0\), use the no-covariate growing-outcome-resolution construction rather than setting \(d=0\) in the conditional tuning rule. Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\theta_n}\sup_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}\{E(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}\asymp\mathfrak R_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\}.
\]
At equality under the uniform density, the full-sample bias-retaining estimator has the exact benchmark
\[
n\widehat\theta^0_{J_y^0,n}\Rightarrow2\int_0^1\mathbb B(t)^2dt=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{2}{\pi^2k^2}\xi_{1,k}^2,
\]
where \(J_y^0\to\infty\), \(2^{J_y^0}=o(n)\), and \(2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y^0}=o(n^{-1})\). Subtracting \(2\sum_{k\le2^{J_y^0}}(\pi^2k^2)^{-1}/n\) yields the centered chaos. Thus the outcome resolution genuinely grows, the quadratic scale is \(n^{-1}\), and \(\rho_{Q,n}=\rho_{L,n}=n^{-1/2}\). This is the two-sample specialization of the del Barrio--Gin\'e--Utzet weighted quantile-process law.
statements.justification: A separate full-sample estimator is necessary to recover the classical two-sample constant rather than a split-sample direct-sum surrogate.
statements.gap: delBarrioGineUtzet2005 gives the unconditional quantile-process limit but not its role as the \(d=0\) branch of a conditional smoothness--degeneracy frontier.
statements.consumer: The result is the required sanity check and supplies exact simulation critical values when no covariate adjustment is used.

statements.statement: Can the mixed linear--quadratic calibration handle construct \(\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{mix}}\) such that \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{0\le\rho\le1}\inf_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{mix}}\}\ge1-\alpha,\] with expected half-width of order \(\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\) for pilot-feasible \(d\ge1\), order \(\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\) for \(d=0\), and the regular Gaussian width implied by SmoothCOT Theorem 3.2 at each fixed unequal law? The construction must derive uniform spectral-tail, anti-concentration, multiplier-coupling, observable pilot-Hessian, covariance, and anisotropic bias-envelope control from the primitive model class.
statements.justification: Uniform calibration is the genuine unresolved step needed to report one interval without pretesting equality.
statements.gap: ChenFang2019 treats fixed second-order maps, SturmaDrtonLeung2024 Gaussianizes incomplete U-statistics, and AgarwalLuedtke2026 retains fixed entropic damping; none controls a growing unregularized anisotropic Hessian and two bias tails together.
statements.consumer: A positive answer gives one defensible uncertainty report for the \(\mathsf{STAR}\) conditional bound across equality and fixed alternatives.

statements.statement: Let \(U_1,\ldots,U_n\) be independent uniform random variables on \((0,1)\), let \(G_n^{-1}\) be their empirical quantile function, set \(u_n(t)=\sqrt n\{t-G_n^{-1}(t)\}\), and define \(u_n^{\mathrm{tr}}(t)=u_n(t)\mathbf 1\{1/n<t<1-1/n\}\).  Then \(u_n^{\mathrm{tr}}\Rightarrow\mathbb B\) weakly in \(L^2(0,1)\), where \(\mathbb B\) is a standard Brownian bridge.

attestation.note: Transcribed from Theorem 4.1 in the Project Euclid publisher PDF, DOI 10.3150/bj/1110228245; specialized in the node statement to \(g\equiv1\).

statements.statement:
For \(d\ge1\), specialize Definition 4 and Theorem 4 of Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn to scalar outcomes, \(d\)-dimensional covariates, group sizes \(n_0,n_1\), and \(N=n_0\wedge n_1\).  If the outcome and covariate supports are compact, the transport objective is Lipschitz, both conditional kernels are Wasserstein--1 Lipschitz in the covariate, the two arm samples are independent and i.i.d. within arm, and the estimator's covariate coupling obeys
\[
E\!\left[\int\|z_0-z_1\|_2\,d\widehat\pi_{n_0,n_1}(z_0,z_1)\right]\le C_{\widehat\pi}N^{-1/(d+2)},
\]
then its adapted direct conditional-optimal-transport estimator and population value satisfy
\[
E|\widehat V_{n_0,n_1}-V_{\mathrm c}|\le \overline C N^{-1/(d+2)}\log N.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: Under Assp. 4--9 with \(r=1/(d_Z+2\vee d_Y)\), \[\mathbb E[|\widehat V_{n_0,n_1}-V_{\mathrm c}|]\le\overline C\gamma_{d_Y,d_Z}(n_0\wedge n_1),\] where \[\gamma_{d_Y,d_Z}(N)=\begin{cases}N^{-1/(d_Z+2\vee d_Y)}\log N,&d_Y\ne2,\\N^{-1/(d_Z+2\vee d_Y)},&d_Y=2.\end{cases}\]

statements.justification: This theorem-level receipt supplies the precise global direct-COT comparator and the only published premise used in the supplemental median aggregation.
statements.gap: The source gives a global \(L^1\) upper bound, not an equality-local minimax converse, degeneracy law, or all-regime confidence procedure.
statements.consumer: The observable pilot-feasibility corollary checks the source hypotheses on a smooth overlap slice and converts the blockwise \(L^1\) bound into an RMSE envelope.

statements.statement:
Put \(a_y=\min\{s_y,1\}\), \(e=\beta/(2\beta+1)\), \(b=4s_z/(4s_z+d)\), and \(\kappa=2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)\).  For \(d\ge1\), uniform absorption of the H\"older-valid pilot remainder over the declared local-radius range means
\[
\sup_{0\le\rho\le1}
\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{a_y\kappa}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2}
{\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-b}}=O(1).
\]
This absorption holds, with the strict exponent inequalities forced by the logarithmic pilot factor, if and only if
\[
s_z>\frac{3d}{4}
\quad\text{and}\quad
s_y>
\frac{s_z\!\left[11d+4s_z+\sqrt{(4s_z-d)(100s_z+23d)}\right]}
{2(4s_z-3d)(2s_z+d)}.
\]
Equivalently, the second condition is
\[
(4s_z-3d)(2s_z+d)s_y^2-s_z(11d+4s_z)s_y-12s_z^2>0.
\]
Consequently, throughout exactly this region the observable upper bound in \(\text{thm:conditional-minimax-frontier}\) attains the intrinsic frontier uniformly in \(0\le\rho\le1\).  Thus \(s_z=d/4\) is the intrinsic minimax elbow, whereas uniform sharpness of the present observable pilot construction begins only beyond \(s_z=3d/4\) and the displayed outcome-smoothness threshold.  Outside this region the theorem's H\"older-order pilot-remainder bracket remains the conclusion, and equality of its two sides is not asserted.

There is also a supplemental global estimator on the existing class when \(s_z\ge1\).  Choose an odd \(K_n\asymp\log n\), split each arm into \(K_n\) disjoint blocks of size \(N_n=\lfloor n/K_n\rfloor\), and on every block use cells of side \(N_n^{-1/(d+2)}\).  Project each covariate to its cell center; at each occupied center form the empirical conditional outcome law; optimally couple the two projected empirical covariate marginals in Euclidean distance; and integrate the squared Wasserstein distance between the paired empirical conditional outcome laws.  Let the final estimator be the median of these \(K_n\) block values.  Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\left\{E(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm{dir,med}}-\theta_n)^2\right\}^{1/2}
\lesssim n^{-1/(d+2)}(\log n)^{1+1/(d+2)}.
\]
Accordingly, for \(s_z\ge1\) the upper side of the minimax bracket may be sharpened to the minimum of \(\rho^2\), the theorem's pilot-remainder envelope, and this direct-COT envelope.  This supplemental bound neither changes the intrinsic converse nor closes the pilot-dominated bracket in general.
statements.justification: This proposition optimizes the Holder-valid pilot remainder and separates the intrinsic elbow from the sharper threshold required by the observable construction.
statements.gap: Neither comparator derives the equality-local pilot-feasibility phase boundary; the direct-COT theorem supplies only the cited auxiliary global rate.
statements.consumer: An analyst can read off the exact matching region and use the direct-COT envelope when the pilot term dominates.

sampling_model.design: Two independent randomized treatment-arm samples, each of even size \(n=2m\), with deterministic equal folds of size \(m\).
sampling_model.units: Observations are \(W_{a,i,n}=(Y_{a,i,n},Z_{a,i,n})\), with scalar outcome support \([0,1]\) and covariate support \([0,1]^d\).
sampling_model.treatment: Randomized arm membership directly samples the two potential-outcome marginals.
sampling_model.overlap: Propensity overlap is not used; the arm laws share the marginal \(R_n\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For \(d\ge1\), opposite-fold joint and marginal wavelet projections are conditionally normalized and clipped to fixed positive bounds. Their averaged conditional density enters a zero-outcome-mean ridge Galerkin inverse, which defines the observed Hessian, first-order score, diagonal-free kernel, and foldwise variance estimator even off the clipping-inactive event. For \(d=0\), the separate branch uses the full empirical quantile processes.

estimand_functional:
Put \(a_y=\min\{s_y,1\}\).  The Gram-corrected estimator \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y^*,J_z^*,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2[\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}+m^{-1}\sum_{a,i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})+\widehat U_{e,J_y^*,J_z^*,n}]\) has local RMSE at most
\[
\min\!\left\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2\right\}
\]
for \(d\ge1\).  Uniformly over \(0\le\rho\le1\), this equals the lower frontier \(\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\}\) exactly when \(s_z>3d/4\) and
\[
s_y>\frac{s_z\{11d+4s_z+\sqrt{(4s_z-d)(100s_z+23d)}\}}{2(4s_z-3d)(2s_z+d)}.
\]
For \(s_z\ge1\), the median-aggregated blockwise direct-COT estimator in the observable pilot-feasibility corollary additionally has RMSE \(O\{n^{-1/(d+2)}(\log n)^{1+1/(d+2)}\}\), so the available upper envelope is the minimum of this rate, the displayed H\"older-valid pilot-remainder rate, and \(\rho^2\).  Outside the uniform pilot-feasibility region this remains an honest upper bracket, not a matching claim.  For \(d=0\), \(\widehat\theta^0_{J_y^0,n}\) has local RMSE \(\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\}\).

The full classes are incomparable; on overlap slices this note is a restriction.  SmoothCOT gives quadratic stability and a fixed-law regular Gaussian limit but no minimax converse to transfer.

It gives no equality-local law or minimax converse.

The main theorem gives Gaussian limits for changing-kernel quadratic estimators under diffuse-spectrum conditions.
The paper proves failure of ordinary bootstrap methods under first-order degeneracy and validity of derivative-aware corrections for fixed maps.
The paper gives Gaussian multiplier approximation for incomplete U-statistics under mixed degeneracy.
The paper derives a second-order causal Sinkhorn statistic and a fixed-entropic weighted chi-square equality law.

tldr: For \(d\ge1\), conditional squared Wasserstein distance has an anisotropic boundary geometry: inverse ellipticity smooths outcome frequencies while covariate resolution replicates the ordered spectrum. A min--max comparison gives Hilbert--Schmidt norm \(\asymp2^{dJ_z/2}\), outcome bias \(2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}\), and covariate bias \(2^{-2s_zJ_z}\). A fully observed two-fold statistic uses clipped-and-normalized opposite-fold density pilots, a ridge Galerkin inverse, explicit first-order scores, and a diagonal-free second-order kernel. In the pilot-feasible smoothness region, balancing the three scales yields local rate \(\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\}\) and elbow \(s_z=d/4\), matched by the sign-paired converse; the limit statement is an \(n\)-dependent Gaussian-quadratic approximation, with chaos only under \(\ell^2\) spectral convergence. The separate \(d=0\) branch recovers the two-sample del Barrio--Gin\'e--Utzet law and \(n^{-1}\) scale. Uniform mixed-regime calibration remains open.

honest_scope: The model has scalar compactly supported outcomes, equal randomized arm sizes, a shared covariate marginal, positive anisotropic H\"older densities, and known smoothness. The sharp conditional upper and lower frontier is stated for \(d\ge1\) only in the explicit pilot-feasible region; outside it the Rademacher lower bound remains, but no observable upper rate is claimed. The primary limit result is triangular, and a fixed Gaussian-chaos limit requires \(\ell^2\) convergence of normalized spectra and shifts. The \(d=0\) result uses a separate full-sample empirical-quantile branch.
